([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] (2014–2015) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = *Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2015 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2015]]) *Jerry West Award (2015) *First-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] (2015) *Big Ten Freshman of the Year (2015) *[[McDonald's All-American]] ([[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2014) }} '''D'Angelo Russell''' (born February 23, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently closed his college career at the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State University]]. ==High school career== Russell attended [[Central High School (Louisville, Kentucky)|Central High School]] in [[Louisville, Kentucky]] before transferring to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]] after his freshman season.[http://www.kentucky.com/2014/04/02/3175422/mcdonalds-all-american-notes-louisville.html Louisville native Russell gives credit to hometown] He was rated by [[Rivals.com]] as a five-star recruit.[https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-D'Angelo-Russell-127378 Rivals.com bio] ==College career== Russell committed to [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] on June 7, 2013, he chose the Buckeyes over [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].[http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9354242/shooting-guard-dangelo-russell-commits-ohio-state-buckeyes D'Angelo Russell commits to Ohio St.] In his college debut, Russell had 16 points, 6 assists and 4 rebounds. On January 9, Russell grabbed a career high 14 rebounds in a win against Maryland. On January 21, Russell scored a career high 33 points in a 69-67 win over Northwestern. On February 8th, in a 79-60 win against Rutgers, Russell recorded a triple double (23 points, 11 rebounds, 11 assists). This was the first triple double recorded by an Ohio State freshman.[http://www.cleveland.com/osu/index.ssf/2014/11/sam_thompson_no_20_ohio_state.html Sam Thompson, No. 20 Ohio State roll over Lowell, 92-55, in season opener] Russell had an impressive showing against 7 seed VCU in the NCAA tournament, scoring 28 points and leading his team to the victory, although his season ended shortly after as the Buckeyes fell to Arizona 73-58. He finished 5th in the voting for the [[John R. Wooden Award]].
